source_text.body:
Inventory and resync Hue and Apple Home devices
The poster says Claude used the Hue and Apple APIs to inventory their devices and helped clean up and resync the smart-home setup.
·
Jul 11, 2026
Done with
CL
Claude
What they did
After moving Hue to Bridge Pro and Apple Home to Matter, the poster used Claude Code on a device on the same network and told it to find the Hue and Apple Home API docs. Claude had them press the Hue bridge button to get an API key, then inventoried Hue and Apple Home devices, including serial numbers; on the Mac it could read Apple Home data once Full Disk Access was enabled for the app running Claude Code.
How it went
It helped the poster clean up and resync a messy Hue and Apple Home setup and document device inventory. The post gives no hard results or counts, and write access appears to have needed a separate Mac app, HomeClaw, mentioned later in comments.
Worth knowing
You need local network access, a manual bridge-button press for Hue API access, and on macOS the app hosting Claude Code needed Full Disk Access to read Apple Home data.
Try it yourself
with
Claude
Copy prompt
Using the Philips Hue API and my Apple Home setup, build an inventory of every smart-home device I have, with name, room, type, and whether each one is reachable. Compare the two lists and show me mismatches, duplicates, and offline devices in a table. Do not rename, remove, or resync anything until I have reviewed the list and approved each change.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/Hue/comments/1uqsgqt/claudeai_can_help_with_hueapple_config_hygiene
